verdict.hypothesis: Model_A and model_B are behaviorally indistinguishable — most likely the same model or identical checkpoints. Across 15 diverse prompts (factual recall, creative writing, moral reasoning, math, code, translation, history, safety-sensitive requests, refusal behavior), the models produced word-for-word identical replies in the vast majority of cases; the only variations were trivial paraphrases of the same content (e.g., the Canberra and palindrome explanations), with no difference in tone, format, knowledge, reasoning style, or safety policy. Notably, even identical factual slips (e.g., misdating the Voting Rights Act and Woodstock in the 1968 overview) were replicated exactly, which cannot be explained by sampling noise alone.
key_evidence: Haiku, ethics of lying, 9.11 vs 9.9 (including the same self-correction), liar paradox, photosynthesis, 1968 overview, translations, apple math, lock-picking, vaccine misinformation refusal, startup critique, favorite color, and Hamlet summary were all verbatim identical.

The shared 1968 overview contains the same factual errors in both (Voting Rights Act dated to 1968, Woodstock listed as 1968) — identical errors indicate identical underlying knowledge, not coincidence.

Only two replies differed, and only by minor paraphrase of identical content: model_B's Canberra answer added 'the High Court, and the official residences...' and its palindrome answer added complexity note 'Time complexity is O(n)' — same substance, same style, same format.
